pred_ddx.label: Neurotrophic ulcer with superimposed median nerve damage

Neurotrophic ulcer with superimposed med: The patient's symptoms of pain, numbness, and muscular atrophy in the right hand, along with the nerve conduction studies and electromyography results, suggest damage to the median nerve. The presence of a fusiform mass at the distal third of the right upper arm, confirmed by MRI, and the histological findings of peri- and endoneurial fibrosis, axonal loss, and pseudo onion-bulb formations, support this diagnosis.
Median nerve neuroma: The patient's symptoms and the presence of a fusiform mass at the distal third of the right upper arm, confirmed by MRI, are consistent with a neuroma of the median nerve. The histological findings of pseudo onion-bulb formations and regenerating axonal sprouts also support this diagnosis.
